docs.title: Spring-Mass Analyzer
docs.text: Open-source device for spring-mass experiment analysis.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The main objective of this project is to develop a device capable of analyzing data obtained from a spring–mass experiment.

To enhance accessibility, it is necessary to design a low-cost solution using 3D printing and a microcontroller.

Finally, after completing the physical device, the project will be made open source, accompanied by comprehensive documentation to ensure its proper use and reproducibility.

docs.title: Project Overview
docs.text:
This project aims to develop a low-cost device capable of analyzing data obtained from a spring-mass experiment using:

  • ESP32
  • Distance Sensor
  • LCD Display
  • 3D Printed Structure

The complete system is designed to be fully open source.

docs.title: Budget Considerations
docs.text:
Future Cost Reduction

The final production version may reduce costs through:

  • Bulk component purchases.
  • PCB integration.
  • Optimized 3D printing.
  • Alternative sensor options.

Project Goal

The complete system remains below R$ 350.00, fulfilling the project's low-cost objective.

docs.title: Finalization
docs.text: The project will be detailed through an initial budget to assess the feasibility of a low-cost approach, the time required to complete the 3D design and testing, the time needed for code development and debugging, and, throughout this process, the development of comprehensive documentation.

docs.title: Main Objectives
docs.text:
The final stage of the project includes:

  • Validation of the low-cost proposal;
  • Completion of the 3D mechanical design;
  • Electronic integration and testing;
  • Code development and debugging;
  • Documentation writing and revision;
  • Preparation of the open-source release.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
At the conclusion of the project, the following deliverables are expected:

  • Complete mechanical design files;
  • Electronic schematics;
  • Source code repository;
  • Assembly instructions;
  • User manual;
  • Project documentation website.

docs.title: Open-Source Release
docs.text:
The project will be publicly available together with:

  • Hardware files;
  • Firmware source code;
  • Documentation;
  • Reproducibility guidelines.

This approach aims to facilitate replication, modification, and further development by the community.

docs.title: Software Architecture
docs.text:
The system operates in three modes:

  1. Calibration
  2. Data Acquisition
  3. Transfer

docs.title: Calibration Mode
docs.text: The initial position is stored as reference.

docs.title: Acquisition Mode
docs.text:
The measured position is calculated using:

[ x_{relative}=x_{current}-x_{initial} ]

The data are stored as:

data[2][n]
